draft.title: The price mechanism
card: The price mechanism is how a market sets prices. It settles on the equilibrium price, where the amount buyers want equals the amount sellers offer.
the price is below equilibrium, so buyers want more than sellers offer. Buyers compete for the limited goods, which pushes the price up.
the price is above equilibrium, so sellers offer more than buyers want. Sellers are left with unsold stock and cut prices, which pushes the price down.
Prices keep moving until the shortage or surplus is gone. The market then settles at the equilibrium price.

4.alt: A demand curve and a supply curve cross at the equilibrium price. At a higher price, sellers offer more than buyers want: the gap between the curves is a surplus. At a lower price, buyers want more than sellers offer: the gap is a shortage.

draft.remember: Shortage: price rises. Surplus: price falls. Both end at equilibrium.

a.q: A market has a surplus at its current price. Which statement describes it?
opts: Sellers offer more than buyers want to buy
Buyers want more than sellers offer
Buyers want exactly what sellers offer
The price is below the equilibrium price
a.why: A surplus means sellers offer more than buyers want at the current price, so stock is left unsold. Buyers wanting more than sellers offer describes a shortage, which is the reverse.
a.clue: Think about who is left with goods they cannot sell.

b.q: Mia sells fresh mangoes at a market stall in Coffs Harbour, NSW. At $4 each, she has 80 mangoes left at the end of the day. If the market keeps adjusting, what will most likely happen to the price?
opts: It falls, because $4 is above the equilibrium price
It rises, because $4 is below the equilibrium price
It stays at $4, because Mia sets the price
It rises, because there are goods left to sell
b.why: Unsold mangoes mean Mia offered more than buyers wanted at $4, which is a surplus. A surplus shows the price is above equilibrium, so sellers cut prices until it clears. Leftover goods do not push prices up.
b.clue: Leftover stock means sellers offered more than buyers wanted.

a.best: Sellers offer more than buyers want to buy

b.best: It falls, because $4 is above the equilibrium price
